An expressed oncogenic NTRK fusion is a TRK-inhibitor biomarker in qualifying advanced solid tumors; larotrectinib criteria include prior progression or no satisfactory alternatives and absence of known acquired TRK resistance mutations.

curation_notes: Original Jones 2013 full-text verification remains pending; FDA review provides an explicitly identified literature lead.

entries.label: IGH / MYC

sections.text: The rearrangement places MYC under immunoglobulin regulatory control, increasing MYC expression and proliferative transcription. It is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma but also occurs in other B-cell neoplasms.

curation_notes: No universal adverse prognosis assigned to isolated MYC rearrangement; Burkitt and double-hit lymphomas are separate diagnostic settings.

entries.label: IGH / BCL2

sections.text: The t(14;18) rearrangement places BCL2 under immunoglobulin regulatory control, increasing antiapoptotic BCL2 expression. It is characteristic of conventional follicular lymphoma and occurs in other germinal-center-derived B-cell lymphomas.
Concurrent MYC and BCL2 rearrangements in large B-cell lymphoma define an aggressive molecular group; this is distinct from isolated IGH/BCL2 rearrangement in follicular lymphoma.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / BCL6
tumor_contexts: B-cell lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

sections.text: The rearrangement substitutes immunoglobulin regulatory elements for normal BCL6 control, sustaining BCL6-dependent transcriptional repression. BCL6 rearrangements occur in several B-cell lymphomas and are not specific to one histologic type.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / CCND1

sections.text: The t(11;14) rearrangement increases cyclin D1 expression through IGH regulatory control and promotes cell-cycle progression. It is characteristic of mantle cell lymphoma and also defines a major plasma cell myeloma subgroup.

curation_notes: No universal prognosis or venetoclax recommendation is made across mantle-cell and plasma-cell disease.

entries.label: IGH / CCND2

sections.text: Immunoglobulin enhancer juxtaposition increases CCND2 expression and can substitute for cyclin D1 activation in a subset of cyclin D1-negative mantle cell lymphomas. These events require an appropriate mantle-cell morphologic and phenotypic classification.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / MALT1
tumor_contexts: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of MALT

sections.text: The t(14;18) involving MALT1 increases MALT1 expression through IGH regulatory control and activates NF-kappaB-associated survival signaling. It is distinct from the t(14;18) involving BCL2.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / BCL10
tumor_contexts: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of MALT

sections.text: The t(1;14) increases BCL10 expression and promotes signaling through the BCL10-MALT1/NF-kappaB pathway. It is a recurrent regulatory rearrangement in MALT lymphoma.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / CRLF2

sections.text: IGH regulatory elements drive CRLF2 overexpression, increasing cytokine-receptor signaling, often with cooperating JAK-pathway lesions. The event occurs in B-ALL and is enriched in Ph-like disease.

curation_notes: CRLF2 expression alone does not prove this rearrangement; no approved JAK-inhibitor indication is inferred.

entries.label: P2RY8::CRLF2

sections.text: A pseudoautosomal-region deletion joins the P2RY8 promoter to CRLF2 coding sequences, increasing CRLF2 expression. It is a promoter-substitution event that can cooperate with JAK-pathway alterations in B-ALL.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / DUX4

sections.text: Insertion or rearrangement of the repetitive DUX4 locus into IGH regulatory architecture causes abnormal DUX4 expression and a distinctive B-ALL transcriptional program, frequently with secondary ERG alterations.

DUX4-rearranged childhood B-ALL generally has favorable outcomes in reported cohorts, despite frequent IKZF1 alterations; this is a subtype-level observation rather than a conclusion from ERG deletion alone.

curation_notes: The repetitive DUX4 locus requires assay-specific mapping review; no single universal IGH/DUX4 junction is asserted.

entries.label: TCR loci / TAL1

sections.text: T-cell-receptor regulatory rearrangements can activate TAL1 expression in developing T cells, disrupting normal lineage-specific transcription. This is an enhancer-driven oncogenic mechanism in T-ALL rather than an asserted chimeric TCR protein.

curation_notes: Exact TRA/TRD/TRB partner and breakpoint must be supplied for an assayed event; this record is a categorical locus group.

entries.label: GATA2 enhancer / MECOM

sections.text: The rearrangement relocates a GATA2 hematopoietic enhancer to MECOM/EVI1, driving EVI1 overexpression while reducing normal GATA2 expression. Its oncogenic mechanism combines enhancer hijacking with GATA2 insufficiency and does not require a GATA2::MECOM coding fusion.
AML with inv(3)/t(3;3) is in the adverse genetic-risk group under adult ELN 2022 intensive-treatment criteria.

curation_notes: Locus label describes a regulatory event; no chimeric coding product is asserted.

entries.label: IGH / FGFR3 and NSD2

sections.text: The t(4;14) rearrangement places IGH regulatory elements near NSD2 and FGFR3, increasing NSD2-associated chromatin activity and, in many cases, FGFR3 signaling. Some tumors lose FGFR3 expression while retaining NSD2 deregulation.

curation_notes: Not one chimeric kinase fusion; risk assessment must use the applicable current myeloma system and co-lesions.

entries.label: IGH / MAF

sections.text: t(14;16) places MAF under IGH regulatory control, increasing a lineage-altering transcriptional program. It is a recurrent primary IGH translocation in plasma cell myeloma.

curation_notes: Historical adverse-risk associations differ from newer co-lesion-based risk definitions; no unqualified contemporary risk assignment included.

entries.label: PRCC::TFE3

sections.text: The fusion retains the TFE3 DNA-binding and dimerization regions while altering its amino-terminal regulatory architecture, producing abnormal MiT/TFE transcriptional activity. PRCC::TFE3 is a recognized TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma fusion.

curation_notes: No prognosis or treatment response assigned solely from the partner.
